episodes.193277: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a boundary over northeast Oklahoma and southeast Kansas on August 15, 2024, with thunderstorms developing just north of and along Interstate 44 by the evening. These storms persisted into the early morning hours of August 16, 2024, resulting in heavy rainfall measuring between 3.25 and 5.49 inches primarily east of Highway 65 in Webster, Wright, Howell, and Texas counties. Flash flooding occurred at multiple locations in Webster County, with areal flooding in Ozark, Douglas, and Texas counties. As the early morning hours progressed, these storms continued to push southeast out of the area by sunrise.||Later in the day, an east to west oriented frontal boundary stalled across south-central Kansas and Missouri, resulting in enough instability and deep layer shear for storms to initiate over Kansas during the early afternoon and push into southeast Kansas by the evening. As the storms moved into southwest Missouri, damaging winds up to 70 mph resulted in numerous reports of trees down in Newton, McDonald, Barry, and Taney counties.
episodes.193278: An east to west oriented frontal boundary stalled across south-central Kansas and Missouri, resulting in enough instability and deep layer shear for storms to initiate over Kansas during the early afternoon of August 16, 2024. Between 6:25 PM and 6:35 PM that evening, thunderstorms were pushing into Cherokee County, with 80 mph winds measured by emergency management. These winds resulted in multiple reports of barns and metal buildings either damaged or destroyed, as well as golf ball size hail.
episodes.193288: A line of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon ahead of a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.193289: A line of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon ahead of a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.193290: A third consecutive afternoon of isolated thunderstorms developed across the region. Very hot temperatures allowed storms to initially develop in the central and southern Texas Panhandle and slowly move southeastward. A dry sub-cloud layer allowed these storms to produce strong wind gusts as the surface. Some of these isolated storms became severe with several Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet sites recording severe wind gusts. A wake low developed within the stratiform region of departing thunderstorms and generated a severe wind gust of 59 mph near Friona (Parmer County) measured by the Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet.
episodes.193291: An isolated and near stationary thunderstorm developed over Cannon AFB August 17th. This storm produced a downburst severe thunderstorm wind gust over the base.
episodes.193313: Gusty showers and thunderstorms across much of Carbon County, Wyoming resulted in reported wind gusts of 60 to 70+ mph on the evening of the 17th.
episodes.193315: Isolated to scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the midday hours south of a pre-frontal trough axis just north of the WFO Huntsville, AL forecast area. These storms progressed east ahead of this boundary across north central and northeastern Alabama producing areas of widespread damaging winds and a isolated hail up to 1 inch in diameter. The strongest storms affected Morgan, Madison, Jackson, and Marshall counties.
episodes.193316: Isolated to scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the midday hours south of a pre-frontal trough axis just north of the WFO Huntsville, AL forecast area. These scattered storms produced large areas of tree damage in Franklin county, TN.
episodes.193326: While a low pressure system spun over the Great Lakes region, active weather extended down into the Middle Ohio Valley and Central Appalachians. Disturbances embedded in this system provided support for showers and storms across the area. An initial round of sub-severe activity occurred with the passage of one such disturbance early on August 17th. Following a brief break, more robust convection began to develop in Ohio and Kentucky as a second upper disturbance moved overhead that afternoon. Broken lines of showers and storms progressed toward the Ohio River by mid-afternoon, downing a tree and power lines in Carter County before storms pushed east into West Virginia.
episodes.193327: While a low-pressure system spun over the Great Lakes region, active weather extended down into the Middle Ohio Valley and Central Appalachians. Disturbances embedded in this system provided support for showers and storms across the area. An initial round of sub-severe activity occurred with the passage of one such disturbance early on August 17th. Following a brief break, more robust convection began to develop in Ohio and Kentucky as a second upper disturbance moved overhead that afternoon. Broken lines of showers and storms progressed toward the Ohio River by mid-afternoon, downing a tree and power lines in Vinton County before storms pushed east into West Virginia.
episodes.193329: While a low-pressure system spun over the Great Lakes region, upper troughing extended down into the Middle Ohio Valley and Central Appalachians. Disturbances embedded in this upper trough provided support for showers and storms across the area. An initial round of sub-severe activity occurred with the passage of one such disturbance early on the 17th. Following a brief break, more robust convection began to develop in Ohio and Kentucky as a second upper disturbance moved overhead that afternoon. Broken lines of showers and storms progressed toward the Ohio River by mid-afternoon, then pushed into West Virginia. While activity tapered off to the north, strong to severe storms marched east across the southern part of West Virginia. Wind damage from these storms resulted in downed trees and power lines across portions of Wayne and Mingo Counties during the afternoon and early evening hours. Activity then continued east and began to diminish in intensity during the evening.
episodes.193375: A period of northwest flow persisted across Central Alabama for a few days in mid-August, with a ridge over the southwestern United States and an upper low over the Great Lakes. A storm in Cherokee County produced damage on August 16, and storms the next day produced damage across central and eastern counties. On August 18, numerous thunderstorms passed through central and southern counties in Central Alabama, producing widespread tree damage and several instances of hail. A couple areas in Coosa and Tallapoosa counties saw hail up to golf ball size.
episodes.194195: Thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall that led to isolated instances of flooding.
episodes.194200: An off-cut-low pressure system over the Pacific NW along with a high pressure system over the Texas Panhandle formed a southwesterly flow over eastern Nevada with monsoonal moisture, creating afternoon thunderstorms that produced high winds.
episodes.194313: A slow-moving upper low over northern Lake Michigan shifted east while the the approach of a pre-frontal trough and destabilization resulted in convective development along and ahead of a cold frontal boundary. Colder and drier mid-levels allowed for MLCAPE  values near 1000-2000 J/kg and mid-level lapse rates of 6-6.5 C/km. Effective shear was marginal, with values between 20 and 30 kts.
episodes.194314: A slow-moving upper low over northern Lake Michigan shifted east while the the approach of a pre-frontal trough and destabilization resulted in convective development along and ahead of a cold frontal boundary. Colder and drier mid-levels allowed for MLCAPE  values near 1000-2000 J/kg and mid-level lapse rates of 6-6.5 C/km. Effective shear was marginal, with values between 20 and 30 kts.
episodes.194350: A slow-moving upper low centered over northern Lake Michigan slowly shifted east during the afternoon, and the approach of a pre-frontal trough combined with diurnal destabilization resulted in convective development along and ahead of a cold frontal boundary.  MLCAPE values near 1000-2000 J/kg and mid-level lapse rates of 6-6.5 C/km resulted in a damaging wind threat with convection.
episodes.194432: A remnant quasi-stationary boundary remained across portions of northern Oklahoma during the day on the 16th. Widely scattered diurnal convection emerged across the aforementioned area. Similar to the 15th (see separate entry), multi-cell thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts and a few reports of hail across portions of western into northern Oklahoma.
episodes.194433: A modest low-level jet during the early morning of the 17th promoted widely scattered thunderstorm development across east-central Oklahoma. Sufficient wind shear and instability promoted a few brief strong to marginally severe thunderstorms, with a damaging downburst event noted west of the community of Ada, Oklahoma.
episodes.194503: A lone thunderstorm developed in Kit Carson county during the afternoon hours producing a 62 mph wind gust and penny size hail.
episodes.195195: Monsoonal moisture moving northward encountered and advancing shortwave and brought strong to severe thunderstorms to southern and central Wyoming. The strongest wind gusts occurred in the higher elevations with a maximum wind gust of 81 mph at Red Canyon in the Wind River Mountains. Wind gusts over 60 mph were reported in portions of Sublette, Sweetwater and Fremont Counties.
episodes.195203: A line of thunderstorms produced instances of wind damage, mostly to trees, across parts of northeast Illinois during the evening of the 16th.
episodes.195204: A line of strong thunderstorms produced one instance of wind damage near DeMotte during the evening of the 16th.
episodes.195205: A line of marginally severe thunderstorms across northern Illinois remained strong as they moved over Lake Michigan during the evening of the 16th.
episodes.195232: A deep area of low pressure centered offshore of Oregon produced moderate to heavy showers and thunderstorms.
episodes.195367: A thunderstorm producing gale-force winds glanced a small portion of the middle tidal Potomac River during the late afternoon hours.
episodes.195384: A few severe thunderstorms produced very localized wind damage over portions of northern Virginia in the greater Fredericksburg area, and over the northwestern suburbs of Washington DC.
episodes.195385: A few severe thunderstorms produced very localized wind damage over portions of northern Virginia in the greater Fredericksburg area, and over the northwestern suburbs of Washington DC.
episodes.195401: A tropical wave increased moisture and instability, giving an extra boost to the typical weather pattern. On Saturday (17th), this promoted unsettled conditions with the formation of strong afternoon thunderstorms.
episodes.195440: Scattered strong to severe storms impacted much of south central and southeast Kansas during the evening hours of August 16th. This activity last until the early morning hours of August 17. The strongest of these storms produced up to baseball sized hail in Cowley County and up to 80 mph winds in Montgomery County.
episodes.195463: A fairly typical summertime upper level pattern was in place with strong high pressure centered well west of the local area. That put southern Louisiana on the eastern periphery of this ridge in a region of northwestern upper level flow. That setup is often conducive for strong to severe thunderstorm development and what took place on August 17th. Using WPC surface/satellite composite analysis, you can backtrack the convection from an MCS that developed in southeastern Wyoming on the early morning hours of August 16th. In short, it tracked across Nebraska and Kansas on the 16th, through Missouri to Mississippi on the 17th. Daytime heating on the 17th reinvigorated the residual MCS boundary as it moved into the coastal waters.
episodes.195478: High pressure was over Texas in tandem with northwesterly flow on the east side of the high brought a disturbance through Arkansas leading to severe thunderstorms that tracked from northwest to southeast across the state. At the surface, a cold front boundary provided a lifting mechanism for the thunderstorms as the boundary moved from north to south across the state.
episodes.195489: In the days prior to August 17th, a dome of high pressure had been in control of eastern Utah and western Colorado, with a plume of monsoonal moisture well to the west in the Central Great Basin. As a strong Pacific trough moved in the Pacific Northwest, the entire system of high pressure and monsoonal plume were nudged eastward, pushing the plume into eastern Utah. Surface layers remained dry, as it often takes several days of monsoonal moisture to saturate the atmosphere. This setup favors strong to severe winds with any shower or thunderstorm that forms.
episodes.195518: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed into northeastern Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 16th, and became more widespread across the area during the evening and overnight hours. The atmosphere became very unstable during the late afternoon over eastern Oklahoma, and deep layer wind shear increased over the region during the evening with the approach of an upper level disturbance. This environment supported severe thunderstorms, including some supercells, that produced large hail up to hen egg size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195521: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed into northeastern Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 16th, and became more widespread across northwestern Arkansas during the evening and overnight hours. The atmosphere became very unstable during the late afternoon over northwestern Arkansas, and deep layer wind shear increased over the region during the evening with the approach of an upper level disturbance. The strongest thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts as they moved across northwestern Arkansas.
episodes.195771: A couple of decaying mesoscale convective systems moved out of southern Missouri and north central Arkansas and then merged and intensified over the Mid-South during the early morning hours of August 17. 2024. Storms fed on a fairly unstable airmass across the region and were aided by about 30 knots of bulk shear. There were several instances of damaging winds with isolated large hail and flash flooding.
episodes.195772: A couple of decaying mesoscale convective systems moved out of southern Missouri and north central Arkansas and then merged and intensified over the Mid-South during the early morning hours of August 17. 2024. Storms fed on a fairly unstable airmass across the region and were aided by about 30 knots of bulk shear. There were several instances of damaging winds with isolated large hail and flash flooding.
episodes.195773: A couple of decaying mesoscale convective systems moved out of southern Missouri and north central Arkansas and then merged and intensified over the Mid-South during the early morning hours of August 17. 2024. Storms fed on a fairly unstable airmass across the region and were aided by about 30 knots of bulk shear. There were several instances of damaging winds with isolated large hail and flash flooding.
episodes.195822: A strong upper level low pressure system was in place across the Great Lakes region heading into the morning hours of Saturday, August 17. From this a cold front draped southwestward, moving towards the state throughout the day. By the time it reached western Kentucky during the afternoon hours. the warm/unstable airmass ahead of the boundary had already spawned showers and thunderstorms. A line of storms formed ahead of the front and continued to outpace the frontal passage eastward. By the time it reached eastern Kentucky, multiple severe thunderstorm warnings were issued for these strong storms. Throughout the afternoon and evening hours, widespread wind damage occurred in numerous counties. Multiple locations also saw damaging hail.  While the main line of storms fizzled out during the evening hours in the far east, additional discrete thunderstorms continued ahead and all the frontal boundary into the overnight for central and eastern Kentucky.
episodes.195840: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over the North Carolina mountains during the late afternoon and evening, with some storms moving out over the foothills during the evening. A few of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195851: A mature upper low with an embedded shortwave allowed for a couple rounds of scattered severe thunderstorms to cross East Tennessee, with hail and damaging thunderstorm winds occurring.
episodes.195854: Isolated thunderstorms developed over western North Carolina during the late afternoon and evening. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts and marginally large hail.
episodes.195855: Widely scattered thunderstorms and isolated storm clusters moved across upstate South Carolina during the late afternoon and evening. A few of the storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195856: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters moved into northeast Georgia during the evening. A couple of the storms produced damaging wind gusts in the Piedmont.
episodes.195892: An area of strong to severe thunderstorms moved through Cochise and Santa Cruz County resulting in a couple of severe threshold wind gusts.
episodes.195900: A line of thunderstorms moved across North and Central GA through the afternoon and evening hours of the 7th. Generally storm motion was not conducive to tap into shear energy, however a few storms which moved more eastwardly were able to tap into both the instability and shear. The greatest storm damage was reported in Hall and Coweta County where extended swaths of wind damage were noted. Some hail up to ping pong ball sized was also reported in northeast GA, early on in the event.
episodes.195932: A warm front associated with a large area of low pressure over the Central Great Lakes tracked through and east of the area. Clearing skies behind the front and a trough over the region initiated thunderstorms as instability increased through the daytime hours within the warm sector of the system. Overall shear values were strong enough to allow some of the thunderstorms to become strong to severe.
episodes.195963: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced high winds.
episodes.195980: Afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms developed across the northwest and south central portions of the Texas Panhandle. A few of these storms produced wind gusts in excess of 60mph in the Texas Panhandle.
episodes.196049: An upper-level disturbance interacting with a dissipating frontal boundary triggered a few clusters of strong thunderstorms across west-central Illinois during the evening of August 16th.  One of the cells produced gusty winds of around 60mph that blew a large tree branch into powerlines northwest of Groveland in Tazewell County.
episodes.196086: An MCS developed across central Virginia on August 17, producing heavy rain and flash flooding as it slowly moved east.
episodes.196097: Thunderstorms brought severe outflow wind gusts.
episodes.196109: Southerly flow and afternoon instability lead to some severe thunderstorm formation over the southern Cascades. ||The threat of hail from these thunderstorms disrupted wildfire response across the area. Some of the wildfires grounded helicopter and aviation response completely, crews were pulled off of the line, some teams only worked at night, and some not at all. This delay in wildfire response is estimated to cost wildfire management agencies $750,000 across the region that experienced severe thunderstorms.  ||In addition, power outages were reported across the region Pacific Power reporting 6,290 customers without power and Portland General Electric reporting 3,700 customers without power.
episodes.196116: Thunderstorms brought gusty winds to much of Utah and flash flooding to southern Utah.
episodes.196127: Thunderstorms brought severe wind gusts to southwest Wyoming.
episodes.196285: As a surface low moved east across the Great Lakes, its trailing cold front dropped south through the Midwest and towards the Lower Ohio Valley. Multiple rounds of convection worked through central Kentucky. Some of these thunderstorms produced damaging winds, resulting in scattered damage across central Kentucky.
episodes.196292: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across various portions of Mississippi during the afternoons of August 14th, 16th, and 17th. These storms caused scattered wind damage from microbursts.
episodes.196385: At the surface, a low wobbled southeastward from the northwestern Great Lakes to southern Lake Huron during the early evening of the 16th through early evening of the 17th. Simultaneously, the attendant warm front moved northeastward from northern Lake Michigan and central Lake Erie to near the northern shore of Lake Ontario and Upper St. Lawrence River Valley, while the trailing cold front moved eastward from the Upper Mississippi River Valley to central Lake Erie and north-central OH.||Within the warm and moist sector, a cluster of multicell thunderstorms persisted eastward across far-northeast OH and generated isolated straight-line convective wind damage in northern Ashtabula County during the early evening of the 16th. The ambient environment exhibited modest MLCAPE of 500-1000 J/kg, modest effective bulk shear of 20-25 knots, and modestly-steep low-level lapse rates near 7C/km. ||During the afternoon through early evening of the 17th, additional multicell thunderstorms developed and persisted northeastward or eastward across north-central and northeast OH, along and ahead of the cold front. These storms generated isolated severe hail and scattered straight-line convective wind damage. Despite modest MLCAPE of 750-1000 J/kg and effective bulk shear near 25 knots, strong convective wind gusts were aided by a corridor of steep low-level lapse rates of 7.5-8C/km. Torrential rainfall was observed in several locations, with flash flooding reported in and near Ravenna where slow storm motions and repeated thunderstorms impacted the area. Precipitable water values of 1.6-1.75 inches resided in the warm and moist sector.
episodes.198941: At the surface, a low wobbled southeastward from the northwestern Great Lakes to southern Lake Huron during the early evening of the 16th through early evening of the 17th. Simultaneously, the attendant warm front moved northeastward from northern Lake Michigan and central Lake Erie to near the northern shore of Lake Ontario and Upper St. Lawrence River Valley, while the trailing cold front moved eastward from the Upper Mississippi River Valley to central Lake Erie and north-central OH.||Within the warm and moist sector, a cluster of multicell thunderstorms persisted eastward along the shore of far-northeast OH and generated a gale-force peak convective wind gust at Conneaut Breakwater Light during the early evening of the 16th. These storms occurred in an environment with weak MUCAPE and moderate effective bulk shear. During the early afternoon through early evening of the 17th, additional multicell thunderstorms developed and persisted northeastward or eastward over and near the southern shore of Lake Erie, along and ahead of the cold front. These storms generated isolated gale-force peak convective wind gusts amidst moderate MUCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively.
episodes.198944: At the surface, a low drifted eastward across southern Lake Huron during the afternoon through early evening of the 17th. The attendant warm front moved northeastward across the Lake Ontario region and toward the Upper St. Lawrence River Valley. Simultaneously, the attendant cold front moved eastward from southeastern Lower MI and northwest OH to central Lake Erie and north-central OH as northwest PA remained within the warm and humid sector. Scattered multicell thunderstorms impacted northwest PA during the early afternoon through early evening hours. The storms generated isolated straight-line convective wind damage amidst moderate MUCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively.
